item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "0d47b77afa3c4929f237bc11dedb29e5f06d2a68272e464c402cdb2ba7217e8f",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "For every real x and t and every admissible state u, the principal matrix at (x,t,u) has a basis of real eigenvectors with real eigenvalues.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines governing.IsHyperbolic; its requirement applies at all real space and time coordinates but only to admissible states.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "Projects the admissible-state set from an equation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies membership requirements for both constant states and the state domain of hyperbolicity.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "Projects the forcing function, taking real x, real t, and a state to a real vector.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the right-hand side of the vector equation and the subtracted term in the residual.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "LocalDef004",
      "meaning": "Projects the principal matrix function of x, t, and state.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the matrix whose eigenbasis determines hyperbolicity and which multiplies qx.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "LocalDef005",
      "meaning": "The residual is qt + A(x,t,u) qx - f(x,t,u), with vector operations performed componentwise.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes residual zero equivalent to qt + A(x,t,u) qx = f(x,t,u) for arbitrary arguments.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "LocalDef006",
      "meaning": "The problem data type, with a governing equation and a real-coordinate-to-state initial function, as exhibited by its constructor and projections.",
      "effect_on_target": "The outer problem binder ranges over such data; no solution or proof of hyperbolicity is required to construct a problem.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "LocalDef007",
      "meaning": "There exist left and right states satisfying IsRiemannWithStates and unequal as vectors.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines IsJumpRiemann and its distinction between equal and unequal half-line states.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "LocalDef008",
      "meaning": "There exist left and right states satisfying IsRiemannWithStates.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines IsRiemann without requiring distinct states.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "LocalDef009",
      "meaning": "The governing equation is hyperbolic, both specified states are admissible, and the initial function equals the left state for x < 0 and the right state for x > 0.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the complete meaning of IsRiemannWithStates, leaving the value at zero unrestricted.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "LocalDef010",
      "meaning": "Constructs a problem with the supplied governing equation and initial data equal to leftState for x < 0, origin for x = 0, and rightState for x > 0.",
      "effect_on_target": "The last assertion concerns this newly constructed problem, using only the original problem's governing equation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "LocalDef011",
      "meaning": "Projects a problem's governing equation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the admissible set, principal matrix, forcing, residual, and equation retained in the constructed problem.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "LocalDef012",
      "meaning": "Projects a problem's initial function from real coordinates to state vectors.",
      "effect_on_target": "This function is constrained on the two open half-lines in the Riemann predicates.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "LocalDef013",
      "meaning": "The equation data type, consisting of an admissible-state set, a principal matrix function, and a forcing function, as exhibited by its constructor and projections.",
      "effect_on_target": "Encodes equation coefficients and a selected state domain without requiring regularity or hyperbolicity.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "LocalDef014",
      "meaning": "Constructs problem data from a governing equation and an initial function.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the piecewise initial function to be paired with the original governing equation without additional hypotheses.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "LocalDef015",
      "meaning": "For a real square matrix A, there exist real eigenvalues indexed by the coordinate index type and a basis b of the real vector space, indexed by that same type, such that A b_p = lambda_p b_p for every p.",
      "effect_on_target": "Hyperbolicity requires diagonalizability over the reals; repeated eigenvalues are allowed.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "LocalDef016",
      "meaning": "A function equals the specified left state at every negative real argument and the specified right state at every positive real argument.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the exact pointwise initial-data requirement, with no condition at zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "LocalDef017",
      "meaning": "The function taking the left state on negative arguments, the right state on positive arguments, and valueAtOrigin at zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the constructed initial data; origin denotes a state value, not a spatial location.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D018",
      "name": "LocalDef018",
      "meaning": "Constructs equation data from any state set, any principal matrix function of x, t, and state, and any forcing vector function of those arguments.",
      "effect_on_target": "Confirms that admissibility, coefficient regularity, and forcing restrictions are not built into construction.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D019",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires all three main assertions, and every listed conjunct within their conditions and conclusions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D020",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Vector equalities are equalities of functions, hence equality of every coordinate; initial-data equalities are exact.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D021",
      "name": "Exists",
      "meaning": "Existential quantification over a specified type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Quantifies the two constant states and, inside hyperbolicity, eigenvalues and an eigenbasis; inner witnesses may depend on preceding binders.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D022",
      "name": "Fin",
      "meaning": "The type of natural indices strictly below a specified natural number.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fin (m+1) indexes exactly m+1 vector coordinates and matrix rows and columns.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D023",
      "name": "Fin.fintype",
      "meaning": "The finite enumeration of all indices in Fin n.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the finite index set used for matrix sums and finite-dimensional structures.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D024",
      "name": "HAdd.hAdd",
      "meaning": "Addition selected by the applicable addition instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Means natural-number addition in m+1 and componentwise real-vector addition in the residual equation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D025",
      "name": "Iff",
      "meaning": "Logical equivalence, requiring implication in both directions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Both predicate characterizations and the residual identity are equivalences.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D026",
      "name": "LT.lt",
      "meaning": "The strict order selected by the relevant order instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Uses real strict inequalities to select the open negative and positive half-lines.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D027",
      "name": "Matrix.mulVec",
      "meaning": "Matrix-vector multiplication: (Mv)_i is the finite sum over j of M_ij v_j.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the coordinate meaning of the principal term and the eigenvector equations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D028",
      "name": "Membership.mem",
      "meaning": "Membership selected by an instance; its explicit arguments put the container before the element.",
      "effect_on_target": "The displayed membership expressions mean leftState or rightState belongs to the admissible-state set.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D029",
      "name": "Nat",
      "meaning": "The natural numbers including zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "The outer m is arbitrary and nonnegative, so the vector dimension m+1 is positive.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D030",
      "name": "Ne",
      "meaning": "Negation of equality.",
      "effect_on_target": "The jump condition requires unequal vectors, equivalently a difference in at least one coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D031",
      "name": "NonUnitalCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocCommRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets associativity as a required axiom while retaining the operations of a nonunital commutative ring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Part of the instance chain supplying ordinary real arithmetic to matrix-vector multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D032",
      "name": "NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets the commutativity requirement while retaining the underlying ring operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Does not alter the real multiplication or addition used in matrix sums.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D033",
      "name": "NonUnitalNonAssocRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring",
      "meaning": "Retains addition, zero, multiplication, and distributivity from the ring structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the algebraic structure required by Matrix.mulVec without adding a target hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D034",
      "name": "NonUnitalNormedCommRing.toNonUnitalCommRing",
      "meaning": "Forgets norm-related structure and keeps the nonunital commutative ring structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "The matrix operations use real arithmetic; no norm condition appears in the assertion.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D035",
      "name": "NormedCommRing.toNonUnitalNormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Views a normed commutative ring as a nonunital normed commutative ring with the same operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "An instance conversion for real arithmetic, imposing no analytic requirement on the equation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D036",
      "name": "Not",
      "meaning": "Logical negation, defined as implication to falsehood.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses failure of the jump predicate when the constructed half-line states are equal.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D037",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "Interprets a natural numeral in the chosen type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets 1 as a natural number and 0 as either real zero or the zero vector.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D038",
      "name": "Pi.instAdd",
      "meaning": "Addition of functions defined at each argument by addition of their values.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes vector addition componentwise.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D039",
      "name": "Pi.instZero",
      "meaning": "The function whose value at every argument is zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Residual equality to zero means every residual coordinate vanishes.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D040",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Coordinates, state entries, matrix entries, forcing entries, and eigenvalues are real.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D041",
      "name": "Real.instAdd",
      "meaning": "The usual real addition operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies addition in vector expressions and finite matrix sums.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D042",
      "name": "Real.instLT",
      "meaning": "The usual strict order on the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Distinguishes x < 0 and x > 0, excluding zero from both conditions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D043",
      "name": "Real.instZero",
      "meaning": "The real number zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies the splitting coordinate and the coordinate values of the zero vector.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D044",
      "name": "Real.normedCommRing",
      "meaning": "The real numbers equipped with their usual normed commutative ring structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides standard arithmetic for matrix multiplication; the norm and metric do not occur in the proposition's requirements.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D045",
      "name": "Set",
      "meaning": "A set of elements of a type, represented by a predicate on that type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The admissible-state set may be an arbitrary subset of the real state space.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D046",
      "name": "Set.instMembership",
      "meaning": "Set membership given by satisfaction of the set's predicate.",
      "effect_on_target": "Imposes precisely the supplied admissibility predicate on selected states.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D047",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "meaning": "Interprets the numeral 0 using an existing zero element.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves the real and vector zero literals without changing their meaning.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D048",
      "name": "instAddNat",
      "meaning": "Ordinary natural-number addition.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes m+1 the successor dimension.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D049",
      "name": "instHAdd",
      "meaning": "Uses a type's addition as its homogeneous HAdd operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects the displayed addition notation to natural addition and pointwise vector addition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D050",
      "name": "instOfNatNat",
      "meaning": "Interprets each natural-number numeral as itself.",
      "effect_on_target": "The dimension increment is exactly the natural number one.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D051",
      "name": "Fintype",
      "meaning": "A finite type equipped with an exhaustive finite enumeration.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports finite sums and coordinate-indexed bases; here supplied canonically for Fin (m+1).",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D052",
      "name": "HSub.hSub",
      "meaning": "Subtraction selected by the applicable instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Subtracts the forcing vector in the residual.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D053",
      "name": "Matrix",
      "meaning": "A function of a row index and a column index with values in the entry type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The principal coefficient is an (m+1)-by-(m+1) real matrix.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D054",
      "name": "Pi.instSub",
      "meaning": "Pointwise subtraction of functions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Residual subtraction acts separately on each vector coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D055",
      "name": "Real.instSub",
      "meaning": "Real subtraction defined by adding the additive inverse.",
      "effect_on_target": "The residual contains ordinary real subtraction in every component.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D056",
      "name": "instHSub",
      "meaning": "Uses a type's subtraction as its homogeneous HSub operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects residual subtraction to pointwise real-vector subtraction.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D057",
      "name": "Algebra.id",
      "meaning": "The algebra of a commutative semiring over itself, with identity scalar embedding and multiplication as scalar action.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures real scalars act on real entries by ordinary multiplication.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D058",
      "name": "Algebra.toSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts the scalar action from an algebra structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the real scalar multiplication used in eigenvalue equations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D059",
      "name": "CommRing.toNonUnitalCommRing",
      "meaning": "Retains the operations of a commutative ring while forgetting the unit requirement.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports real algebraic operations in dependencies without changing the underlying arithmetic.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D060",
      "name": "CommSemiring.toSemiring",
      "meaning": "Views a commutative semiring as a semiring with the same operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the semiring structure needed for real modules and bases.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D061",
      "name": "DFunLike.coe",
      "meaning": "Coerces a function-like object to its underlying function.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows evaluating the eigenbasis at a coordinate index to obtain a vector.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D062",
      "name": "Function.hasSMul",
      "meaning": "The scalar action on functions induced pointwise from the action on their values.",
      "effect_on_target": "Multiplication of an eigenvector by an eigenvalue is componentwise real scaling.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D063",
      "name": "HSMul.hSMul",
      "meaning": "Scalar multiplication selected by the applicable instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses lambda_p times the basis vector b_p in the eigenvector condition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D064",
      "name": "Module.Basis",
      "meaning": "An indexed basis of a module: a linearly independent family spanning that module.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires a complete real eigenbasis of the state space, not merely a family of eigenvectors.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D065",
      "name": "Module.Basis.instFunLike",
      "meaning": "Evaluates a basis at an index by applying its inverse coordinate representation to the corresponding unit coordinate vector.",
      "effect_on_target": "The vectors in the eigenvector equations are the actual members of the full basis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D066",
      "name": "Pi.Function.module",
      "meaning": "The module structure on a function space obtained from pointwise operations in its codomain.",
      "effect_on_target": "The eigenbasis is a basis of the standard real vector space of coordinate functions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D067",
      "name": "Pi.addCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "The pointwise additive commutative monoid structure on functions.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the standard additive structure on the vector space used by Module.Basis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D068",
      "name": "Real.commRing",
      "meaning": "The usual commutative ring structure of the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the ordinary real operations underlying scalar actions and linear algebra.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D069",
      "name": "Real.decidableLT",
      "meaning": "A decision instance for each strict comparison of real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the piecewise function to branch on x < 0 and 0 < x; it imposes no extra restriction on x.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D070",
      "name": "Real.instAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "The real numbers with their usual additive commutative monoid structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the additive function-space structure required for the eigenbasis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D071",
      "name": "Real.instCommSemiring",
      "meaning": "The real numbers with their usual commutative semiring structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the real self-algebra and its scalar action.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D072",
      "name": "Real.semiring",
      "meaning": "The usual semiring structure on the real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the scalar semiring for the real vector-space basis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D073",
      "name": "Semiring.toModule",
      "meaning": "A semiring viewed as a module over itself, with scalar multiplication given by multiplication.",
      "effect_on_target": "Together with the function-space module, gives the usual real linear structure on states.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D074",
      "name": "instHSMul",
      "meaning": "Uses an existing scalar action as the corresponding HSMul operation.",
      "effect_on_target": "Resolves scalar multiplication in the eigenbasis condition to real-vector scaling.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D075",
      "name": "ite",
      "meaning": "Returns its first value when the condition holds and its second value otherwise.",
      "effect_on_target": "The nested conditionals assign the left state for x < 0, the right state for x > 0, and the origin state exactly at x = 0.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "For every natural number m, put n = m+1, I = {0,...,m}, and V = the real vector space of functions I → R.",
      "For every problem P consisting of governing equation E and initial function g: R → V, write S ⊆ V for E's admissible states, A: R × R × V → Mat_n(R) for its principal matrix function, and f: R × R × V → V for its forcing.",
      "In the first characterization, the existential witnesses L ∈ V and R ∈ V may depend on P and m; R is quantified after L. They are constant states independent of the spatial variable x.",
      "The residual equivalence quantifies independently over all x,t ∈ R and all u,qt,qx ∈ V, outside the existential quantifiers for L and R.",
      "The jump characterization has its own existential witnesses L,R ∈ V, subject to the joint Riemann-with-states and inequality requirements.",
      "The final assertion quantifies universally over L,O,R ∈ V; O is the initial state at the spatial coordinate zero.",
      "Within hyperbolicity, for each x,t ∈ R and u ∈ S there exist lambda: I → R and an I-indexed real basis b of V such that A(x,t,u)b_p = lambda_p b_p for every p ∈ I. These witnesses may depend on x,t,u, and the basis is existentially quantified after lambda."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "There are no outer hypotheses on P beyond its data type and the positive finite dimension n = m+1.",
      "The final universally quantified assertion assumes that E is hyperbolic, L ∈ S, and R ∈ S.",
      "Within that final assertion, the non-jump conclusion assumes L = R, and the jump conclusion assumes L ≠ R."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "P.IsRiemann holds if and only if both of the following hold: (a) there exist L,R ∈ V such that E is hyperbolic, L ∈ S, R ∈ S, g(x) = L for every x < 0, and g(x) = R for every x > 0; (b) for all real x,t and all u,qt,qx ∈ V, residual_E(x,t,u,qt,qx) = 0 if and only if qt + A(x,t,u)qx = f(x,t,u).",
      "P.IsJumpRiemann holds if and only if there exist L,R ∈ V such that P.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R) and L ≠ R.",
      "For every L,O,R ∈ V, if E is hyperbolic and L,R ∈ S, define P' to have governing equation E and initial function g'(x) = L for x < 0, g'(0) = O, and g'(x) = R for x > 0. Then P'.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R), and both implications hold: if L = R then P'.IsJumpRiemann is false; if L ≠ R then P'.IsJumpRiemann holds."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Hyperbolic(E) means that for all x,t ∈ R and u ∈ S, the real matrix A(x,t,u) has an entire basis of real eigenvectors with real eigenvalues.",
      "RiemannWithStates(P,L,R) means Hyperbolic(E) ∧ L ∈ S ∧ R ∈ S ∧ (for every x < 0, g(x) = L) ∧ (for every x > 0, g(x) = R).",
      "Riemann(P) means there exist L,R ∈ V with RiemannWithStates(P,L,R).",
      "JumpRiemann(P) means there exist L,R ∈ V with RiemannWithStates(P,L,R) and L ≠ R.",
      "residual_E(x,t,u,qt,qx) = qt + A(x,t,u)qx - f(x,t,u). Its ith coordinate is qt_i + sum over j ∈ I of A(x,t,u)_ij qx_j - f(x,t,u)_i.",
      "Vector addition, subtraction, zero, and scalar multiplication are componentwise, and vector equality means equality in every coordinate."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every positive finite state dimension and every problem consisting of an equation and initial data, three assertions hold simultaneously. First, being a Riemann problem is equivalent to having two admissible constant states on the negative and positive open half-lines for a governing equation whose principal matrix has a real eigenbasis at every real space-time point and admissible state, together with the universal algebraic equivalence between zero residual and qt + A(x,t,u)qx = f(x,t,u). Second, being a jump Riemann problem is equivalent to possessing such left and right states that are unequal. Third, for any hyperbolic governing equation of the given problem and any admissible left and right states, assigning those states to the respective open half-lines and any state whatsoever at zero produces a Riemann problem with those specified states. This constructed problem is not a jump Riemann problem when the two half-line states are equal, and is a jump Riemann problem when they are unequal."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "The dimension is m+1 ≥ 1; a zero-dimensional state space is excluded, while dimension one is included.",
